question: During a structured adolescent health checkup, after completing the physical examination including SMR staging, the clinician begins the psychosocial screening. Which mnemonic correctly represents ALL domains of the HEEADSSS assessment framework?

answers.text: Home, Eating, Education, Activities, Drugs, Sexuality, Suicide/depression, Safety

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. HEEADSSS covers: Home (family, living situation), Eating (body image, eating patterns), Education/Employment, Activities (peers, hobbies), Drugs (tobacco, alcohol, illicit), Sexuality (orientation, partners, contraception), Suicide/Self-harm/Depression, Safety (violence, accidents, seatbelts). All 8 domains are covered.

answers.text: Home, Exercise, Emotions, Alcohol, Drugs, Sex, Suicide, School

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This is an approximate but incorrect version. 'Exercise' is not a named domain (it falls under Activities); 'Emotions' is not a domain; 'Eating' is a specific named domain. Use the validated HEEADSSS acronym.

answers.text: Health, Eating, Education, Activities, Depression, Sexuality, Smoking, Safety

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The first letter H stands for 'Home' (not 'Health'), and the seventh domain is 'Suicide/depression/self-harm' — not just depression, and 'Drugs' is a specific domain (not limited to smoking).

answers.text: Home, Education, Eating, Alcohol, Drugs, Sex, Self-harm, Sports

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The order is not standard, 'Sports' is not a separate domain (it is part of Activities), and 'Safety' is a distinct validated domain that is absent from this option.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the HEEADSSS framework: Home — Eating — Education/Employment — Activities — Drugs — Sexuality — Suicide/Self-harm/Depression — Safety. Note that Eating is the second domain (body-image issues are screened early), and Safety is the final domain (covering accidents, violence, risky behaviours).

Correct. HEEADSSS is the standard psychosocial screening tool for adolescents. Each domain must be systematically addressed, ideally after establishing a private, confidential relationship with the adolescent. Begin with less sensitive domains (Home, Education, Activities) before moving to Drugs, Sexuality, and Suicide/Safety.
